**GAME OVERVIEW**

**Work in progress title:** Sunken Contract

Singleplayer scuba diving resource management / exploration game with a horror story told through visual novel segments. Takes place over 20 in-game days that alternate between Interior and Excursion gameplay, detailed below. On Excursion days, the player collects tellurium that is converted into credits to be spent in a shop. The player’s goal, which they learn through dialogue on Interior days, is to progress the story fast enough to meet the conditions for the good ending before the 20 days are up. They do this by collecting enough tellurium to purchase key items and exploring enough to find key locations outside the submarine.

**AUDIENCE / USE CASE**

Intended to appeal to fans of atmospheric horror and story-driven mystery games such as *Iron Lung* and *No, I’m Not a Human*. Meant to be played at a desktop computer in focused 1-2 hour long sessions so that the player has adequate time to feel immersed in the setting and story. Conveys tension in both its gameplay systems and plot; playing it should feel somewhat like watching a slow-paced horror movie.

**ART STYLE**

Gritty and semi-realistic; color palette is mostly cool and neutral dark colors.

**Interior Days:** 2D Visual novel style. Static room backgrounds and flat full-body character sprites.

**Excursion Days:** Top-down 2D. Very cool and dark colors. Lighting and water ripple post-processing effects help to evoke an underwater atmosphere and create depth despite the 2D assets.  
**STORY OVERVIEW**

The Company (Trident Excavation) has hired you to spend 20 days aboard the Extreme-depth Submergence Mining Vessel HZ-3280. You will be the foreman, in charge of mining industrial tellurium from the ocean floor. You will be accompanied by three crewmates, each with their own role aboard the submarine. 

**CHARACTERS**

**Player character:** Unnamed blank slate character; the player should feel like they are fully immersed in the scenario. Foreman of the mining operation, i.e. the head tellurium miner. Spends every other day outside the submarine, mining. In charge of contacting the Company and ordering equipment.

**Medic:** Kirsten. The only member of the crew who has been on a submarine before. Highly cautious and particular about keeping tabs on the condition of the vessel and her crewmates. Carries around a clipboard. Mostly found in the shared space, sometimes in the storage closet or lab. The penalty for being incapacitated on excursions changes if she dies.

**Lab worker:** Jonah. Cleans and processes tellurium samples in the lab. Is happy with this position because he has a fear of open water. He only ended up working on a submarine because this was the only job he could find. Mostly found in the lab, sometimes in the shared space or storage closet.

**Apprentice diver:** Cole. Somewhat bitter that the player gets to lead the operation even though the two of them went through the same training program. Sometimes acts defiant and negligent. Goes on short dives on the player’s interior days; passively provides 30-60 credits on each interior day (refer to “interior” section below). Always found in the moonpool. Only present on the submarine after all other living crewmates have been talked to.

**ENDINGS**

**Good ending:** You complete your contract with the Company. When the submarine surfaces, officials burn it and all of its cargo. You and any surviving crew are made to sign an NDA. You are compensated per your contract, but must live with the knowledge that all of that death was for nothing. That is, unless the Company had other motives.

**Bad ending:** You get infected. Possessed by a will and vitality that isn’t your own, you leave the submarine without any breathing or pressure gear and somehow swim far away into the open ocean. Fungal growths root you to the seafloor. The shadow of a leviathan-like creature looms over the husk of what was once you.

**STORY PROGRESSION**

On day 5, Medic finds a strange slimy substance in the lab air filter. They tell the player to watch out for any symptoms, and the player sends a request to the Company to add medicine to the shop.

On the next interior day, 1 medicine is in stock in the shop. The Company says that as a cost cutting measure, they will only provide 1 without photographic evidence that more is needed.

The player can buy and use this medicine whenever they want, but it will only have an effect on an early-stage infection, and it will be wasted otherwise.

An expensive and generally useless camera module for the diving suit has been available in the shop for the whole game. Aside from its quest importance, it only gives a minor boost to the player's flashlight cone size on excursions. If the player buys it, and someone on the submarine has a late-stage infection, the player can use it to take a photo of them. (The late-stage infection causes visible fungal growths on the host)

At the terminal, the player can plug in the camera module to send the photo evidence to the Company.

As they do this, a second window pops up on the terminal, asking for an image-recognition passkey to access encrypted files. A hint for what the image needs to be is given, and it alludes to a particular location on the ocean floor.

The Company's response to the "evidence" photo comes on the following interior day. They say it's not cost effective to use medicine to deal with this infection, and instead they give you permission to eject highly infected crew members from the submarine.

The player can do this, but it doesn't achieve anything except getting the infected crew members outside faster, since they will escape on their own eventually, anyway. (The parasite makes its host want to be outside on the ocean floor, because the parasite wants to be eaten by and infect larger sea animals)

On following excursion days, the player can find the location hinted at in the terminal and use the camera module to "take a photo" of it.

If they return to the terminal with the photo, they can read secret text files about how the parasite works, implying that the Company knew about it all along.

The player learns that if they want to decontaminate the submarine from the early-life-cycle parasite, they need to find a piece of its late-life-cycle form and bring it back onto the submarine. (This sounds nonsensical but the point is to encourage exploring during excursions. I came up with a made-up sci-fi reason why it works.)

So on a following excursion day, the player finds the "husk" of one of their infected crewmates far away from the submarine. There are big mushroom growths sprouting from them. The player can take a piece of the mushroom and bring it back to the submarine.

**Win condition:** This will cure all current infections and give the player the good ending. If they fail to do this before the 20 days are up (cannot afford camera module in time, cannot find passkey/husk in time), they get the bad ending (the player gets infected).

**INFECTION PROGRESSION (KEY DAYS)**

Day 5: Lab Worker gets early-stage infection.  
Progresses to late-stage on day 9  
Lab Worker goes missing on day 13, unless ejected before this.

Day 9: Medic gets early-stage infection.  
Progresses to late-stage on day 13 unless cured with medicine before this.  
If infected, medic goes missing on day 17, unless ejected before this.

Day 13: Apprentice diver gets early-stage infection.  
Progresses to late-stage on day 17 unless cured with medicine before this.

If player has completed the quest before the end of the game (fungus sample brought back to submarine on or before day 20), they will not get infected, and the good ending will be achieved. Otherwise, they will get the bad ending.  
**EXCURSION**

**Equip screen:** At the start of every excursion day, all equippable items are displayed in a grid. The player can click on them to equip and unequip whatever they choose. Equipping a hydrox tank will gray out any other available sizes of hydrox tank; i.e. a player can only equip one size of tank at a time. For items that the player can carry multiples of (mining machines and stimulant canisters), the player can choose exactly how many they will bring. The total weight of equipped items will be displayed on screen (refer to “weight indicator” below). The default loadout will be whatever the player chose on the previous excursion day.

**Loadout at start of game:** 4 mining machines and a light hydrox tank

**Hydrox system:** Player is on a timer based on what size of tank they have equipped (lengths in item table below). If the timer runs out, the screen tints red and the player’s movement speed will drop to 0 over the next 15 seconds. If they don’t reach the submarine before this time is up, they are incapacitated.

**Mining spots (numbers subject to change):** Gradually deplete as they are mined. However, the mining tier information displayed on the screen WILL NOT update until the player re-prospects the mining spot. Thus, a mining machine might be producing less tellurium than it says it is, if the player has not prospected its spot recently.

Tier 1: Gives 1 tellurium every 30 seconds (2t/min). Fully depletes after giving 10 tellurium.  
Tier 2: Gives 1 tellurium every 15 seconds (4t/min). Becomes tier 1 after giving 20 tellurium.  
Tier 3: Gives 1 tellurium every 10 seconds (6t/min). Becomes tier 2 after giving 30 tellurium.  
Tier 4: Gives 1 tellurium every 5 seconds (12t/min). Becomes tier 3 after giving 40 tellurium.  
Tier 5: Gives 2 tellurium every 5 seconds (24t/min). Becomes tier 4 after giving 60 tellurium.

**Prospecting tool:** Player cannot move while it’s in use. Takes 3 seconds to use, during which the player can’t move. After 3 seconds are up, mining spots on the screen will be highlighted and marked according to tier. They will remain marked for the remainder of the game (but their information may be inaccurate if the spot is mined and not regularly re-prospected, as described above.) After use, tool is on cooldown for 5 seconds. If a spot is re-prospected and its tier has changed since it was last prospected, there will be a visual indicator to make this clear to the player.

**Mining machines:** Place on a prospected mining spot to begin mining. Pick it back up to collect the tellurium. If a machine is left out when the day ends, its mining spot will automatically drop a tier. The machine will be broken when the player returns to it. When the player picks it back up, it will not be retrieved, but they will collect 0-80% of the tellurium it harvested.

**Extraction Inventory:**   
The currently equipped size of hydrox tank is written at the top of the screen.   
Underneath is a 8x6 grid of item slots. All equipped items (besides the tank, since it’s required) and items that were collected on this excursion will be found here.   
Mousing over an item shows its description.   
The player can click on a slot containing item(s) and choose how many they want to drop. Dropped items appear on the ground at the player’s position and can be picked up on the same excursion day. Otherwise, they will disappear forever.   
Trying to pick up an item / collect a mining machine when there are no available slots in the inventory will not work and will notify the player that their inventory is full.  
Item stacking info and whether or not an item can be dropped is found in the items tables below.

**UI:**   
Reminder of inventory button  
Hydrox tank indicator  
Radar-style minimap that only shows the direction of the submarine, purchased items, and placed mining machines  
Weight indicator (described below)  
Mining machine icon with a number showing how many mining machines are currently held  
Prospecting tool icon with reminder of its keybind, grayed out when prospector is on cooldown  
If any stimulant canisters were equipped on that day, an icon showing their remaining count and keybind

**Weight/speed system (numbers subject to change):**   
Player’s weight W is the sum of all the weights of the items they equipped E \+ weights of all items they collected on that excursion day C, all over 100\. W \= (C+E)/100  
If W\<.5 then the player’s speed multiplier S is 1\.  
If .5\<=W\<=1 then S \= 1-.5W+.25  
If W\>1 then S \= 1-W+.75

Stimulant Canister speed buff B where t is time in seconds since canister was used:  
B \= \-.025t \+ .5

Multiply the player’s speed constant by: S \+ B \+ (.3 if Advanced Flippers are equipped, 0 if not)

**Weight indicator:** A bar that visually displays W from 0 to 1\. When W\<.5, the bar is green. When .5\<=W\<=1, the bar is yellow. When the W\>1, the bar is red.

**On return to submarine:** If any mining machines are still out, the player is reminded that they will break if left on overnight. The player confirms that they want to end the excursion. Then transition to daily expenses screen.

**On incapacitation:** Brief cutscene with text on screen. Text TBD  
If medic is alive: 70-90% of tellurium in inventory is lost.  
If medic is dead: 100% of tellurium in inventory is lost. 20-50% of mining machines and 20-50% of stimulant canisters in inventory are lost.  
Transition to daily expenses screen.

**Daily expenses screen:** After returning to the submarine or being incapacitated the following information is displayed:

X Tellurium Samples Collected \= 10\*X Credits  
Daily expenses: \-50 Credits (-100 if incapacitated)  
Total credits: (credits in bank) \+ 10\*X \+ (daily expenses)

If the total credits ends up being negative or 0, the player can’t buy any items in the shop until it’s positive again.

**Excursion controls:**   
Swim with WASD.   
Move flashlight with mouse.   
Press TAB to open inventory.  
Press E to prospect.   
Press R to use a stimulant canister if available.  
Left click on a prospected mining spot to place a mining machine.   
Mouse over a mining machine to see how much it has collected.   
Left click a mining machine to pick it up and gather any tellurium it collected.  
Left click on items and quest locations to pick up / interact.  
A button prompt will appear over every clickable object to tell the player what they’re about to do.

**EXTERIOR MAP**  
![][image1]

**INTERIOR**

**Gameplay overview:** Dark background with the current day number. Then transition to map screen. The player can click on a room on the map to move to that room. Rooms contain characters that can be spoken to as well as some interactable objects, like the computer terminal. The terminal is used to access the item shop and also to progress the story at certain points (contacting the Company and accessing encrypted files). The player must talk to all living crew members before ending each day.

**Rooms:**   
Sleeping quarters \- Player can click on the bed to end the day  
Shared space \- Contains interactable computer terminal   
Storage closet  
Processing lab  
Moonpool \- Where the apprentice diver can be found after all other living crewmates have been talked to

**Daily expenses screen:** Since the apprentice diver dives on interior days, the player still receives some credits.  
The following information is displayed after the player goes to sleep, where 3\<=X\<=6 except on day 1, where X=6:

Cole mined X tellurium samples today \= 10\*X Credits  
Daily expenses: \-50 Credits  
Total credits: (credits in bank) \+ 10\*X \+ (daily expenses)

**Interior Inventory:** Different from the excursion inventory. Infinitely long list of all items in the player’s possession. Items with multiples can stack infinitely. Nothing can be used or dropped, it just exists so the player can keep track of what they have and read item descriptions. Lists everything except tellurium samples, since these are converted to credits and deleted when the excursion day ends. Purchased items are not added to this inventory until the player collects them on an excursion day.

**Interior controls:**   
Left click for everything.  
Map and inventory icons are on screen and can be clicked.  
Click on characters and interactable objects to talk/interact.  
**COMPUTER TERMINAL** 

**Overview:** Generally shows two windows: Credit Shop and Contact Management. When the player opens the terminal with a photograph in their inventory, an “uploading photo from camera module” alert will appear. The first time this happens, a third window will appear: Administrator Access.

**Contact Management:** Contains an “inbox” and, at appropriate times in the quest, a button to request medicine from the Company. The player requests medicine on day 5 and receives a message in the inbox on day 7\. Once they get a Photograph of Infected Crewmate, they can request medicine again, and receive a 2nd response on the following interior day.

**Administrator Access:** Appears when the player uploads a photo for the first time. Is “locked”, says that an image-recognition passkey must be uploaded to access encrypted files, and gives a hint. When the player returns to the terminal with a Photograph of the Eye of the Abyss in their inventory, it unlocks, and the player can read information to clue them in to the next step of the quest. Only after doing this can the player collect Full-grown Fungus Pieces from dead crewmates outside the submarine.

**Shop:** Lists all items from the “shop items” table below. Lists their names, descriptions, weights, prices, and how many are in stock. All items from this table will be in stock at the start of the game, except Antimicrobial Medicine, which appears in the shop on day 7\. Stock information is in the table.

Purchased items are not immediately added to the player’s inventory. Instead, they are randomly scattered outside the submarine on the next excursion day. The player must collect them and bring them back to the submarine at the end of the day to claim them, otherwise they disappear. Lost items (that were either bought and not collected, or dropped somewhere outside the submarine) will restock in the shop, but will have to be purchased again.
